title: Why Do Embedded Earth Pressure Cells Under-Register Subgrade Stresses in Accelerated Pavement Tests? A Finite Element Study of Cell–Soil–Box Interaction at the ALT-LIRA Facility
content: Earth pressure cells in the subgrade of the ALT-LIRA circular accelerated pavement testing facility registered 5–10 kPa under a 57.5 kN dual wheel, 10–65% of the vertical stress computed with verified finite element (FE) models of the pavement. This study asks whether the cell, its steel mounting box and the surrounding soil can explain the gap. The installation is only partly documented, so every geometry and stiffness is treated as an assumption. An axisymmetric FE model, verified against  Lamé’s sphere solution, a rigid-punch solution and a three-dimensional model (489 runs), gave the ratio \( R \) of the registered to the free-field stress. A stiff cell of aspect ratio 5.2 over-registered (\( R = 0.9 \)–1.2), alone or in a steel box with intact backfill. \( R \) fell to 0.10–0.65 only with a compliant cell (\( E_c < 0.3E_s \)), a backfill softer than about \( 0.07E_s \) around and below the box, or a soft layer of 20–80 mm in front of the cell face. These conditions are plausible for a hand-dug pit but undocumented, and stiffening of the soft zone under traffic raises \( R \), as the readings did. The readings therefore cannot validate the computed subgrade stress. Bounds, a calibration protocol and installation recommendations are given.
